Application Materials.content:
As part of your online application you will need to upload scanned documents. All academic documentation should be scans of the originals, not photographs. The scans should be complete and of a good quality, showing the 4 corners of all pages of the original document. Please do not merge separate qualifications together. Please do not upload academic documents to the funding section.
Your application must include:
- A copy of your degree certificate and complete transcript. If you are still studying, provide your latest transcript plus a list of modules yet to be studied.
- Evidence of your final or current overall % or GPA.
- A copy of your grading scale/scheme if this is not on your degree transcript.
- CV/Resume: include an up-to-date CV showing your relevant work experience and education.
- CAS, BRP and Visa, for international students that have previously studied in the UK on a student visa.
- If you entered your current degree programme later than year 1, include separate details of the qualification used to gain entry into that later year, including any transcripts and certificates for that qualification.
If you have them, please include:
- Your approved English Language test, if applicable.
- A personal statement. A personal statement is not required as standard, but could strengthen your application in circumstances such as explaining a gap in your education or if your education/degree subject is not directly relevant to the programme. The personal statement should be **no more than one side of A4** and should include details on how your prior studies are linked to your future plans and why you want to study the programme you have applied for.
References are not usually required, but in specific borderline cases a reference may be required to help make a decision.
Country-specific documents:
- Applicants with Chinese degrees: provide evidence of your current/final overall weighted percentage (%); GPA or arithmetic percentage is not accepted.
- Applicants with Indian degrees should include a copy of your bachelor’s degree certificate, consolidated mark sheet, semester mark sheets, University marking scheme, and official evidence of your current/final overall award as a percentage (%). If you have not completed your degree, provide the bottom three items.
- Applicants with Canadian degrees: provide details of the grading system used on your transcript, including the percentage pass mark for your degree. If your degree was taught in English, include official evidence of this.
Supporting documents should always be sent via an enquiry or condition response in the applicant portal so the document links to the correct application automatically.

Interview Requirements.content: We aim to make decisions within **three to five weeks** if all necessary documents have been received. You will be contacted directly if we require any further information or wish to invite you for an interview or audition.

Application Deadlines.content:
Start date: **September 2026**
**Application deadlines**
Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible.
- **31 July 2026** – International applicants
- **11 September 2026** – UK applicants

Academic Requirements.content:
A bachelor degree with a **2:1 (hons)** in a subject containing a substantial mathematical, statistical and/or computing component. Successful applicants will have **strong grades (mainly firsts with no marks below 2:2)** in mathematical modules. You must provide a list of the type and level of maths/computing modules that you have studied if this is not obvious from your transcript. We may ask for further detailed module information if these are not clear on your transcript. We do not normally accept degrees in accountancy or finance for this MSc. We accept a range of [international equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/admissions-qualifications).
For applicants from China: accepted qualifications include **4 year Bachelor degrees**. The University of Leeds uses institutional lists when assessing applications from accepted Chinese institutions, and requirements may vary by school. If the course asks for **2.1**, applicants need **70%-85%, depending on your institution**. If the course asks for **2.2**, applicants need **70%-80%, depending on your institution**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
English language requirements: **IELTS 6.5 overall, with no less than 6.0 in all components**. For other English qualifications, read [English language equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/international-admissions/doc/entry-requirements "English language equivalent qualifications").
International students who do not meet the English language requirements for this programme may be able to study a postgraduate pre-sessional English course, designed with a progression route to the degree programme. Options include [Language for Science (6 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/i204/language-for-science), [Language for Science: General Science (10 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/i203/language-for-science-general-science), the [six week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j615/online-academic-english-presessional-6-weeks-), the [10 week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j614/online-academic-english-presessional-10-weeks-), and longer [postgraduate pre-sessional English courses](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre-courses/doc/masters-pre-sessional-english).

Program Overview.content:
Start date: September 2026. Delivery type: On campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
The Data Science and Analytics MSc addresses the increasing demand for people who can manage, control and provide insight into the way data is used. It develops understanding of computer science and mathematics, alongside familiarity with data needs and processes in areas including healthcare, business, government and the environment. The course offers the opportunity to develop skills in analysing structured and unstructured data, analysing large datasets, critically evaluating results in context, and getting insights from data.
The course combines expertise from the Schools of [Computer Science](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing), [Geography](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/geography) and [Mathematics](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/maths) with [Leeds University Business School](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/), allowing students to benefit from a range of data science perspectives and applications and tailor the course to their career ambitions. Students can choose modules from the School of Mathematics, the School of Computer Science, the School of Geography and Leeds University Business School. Mathematics modules are available for students who are not from a mathematics/statistics background, while computing modules are suitable for students who are not from a computer science background.
The course introduces different perspectives on data science, including the mathematical and computational underpinnings of the subject and its applications in specific contexts. Students put theory into practice through a project focused on a real-world problem, applying knowledge acquired throughout the course and demonstrating independent research skills necessary for a professional or academic career. Many recent projects have involved co-supervision with the Leeds Clinical Trials Unit, Leeds Institute for Data Analytics (LIDA) and the MET office. It is possible to involve an industrial partner in the dissertation, subject to approval of the programme manager.
Research conducted on campus feeds directly into the course, shaping learning in areas such as probability and financial mathematics, modern applied statistics and analysis. Students benefit from close links with organisations including [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/), [Leeds Institute for Fluid Dynamics](https://fluids.leeds.ac.uk/) and the [Alan Turing Institute](https://www.turing.ac.uk/), the UK’s national institute for data science and artificial intelligence.
Teaching is through lectures, tutorials, seminars and supervised research projects, with extensive use of IT and a wide range of materials to enhance and extend formal teaching. The programme team includes academics from the Schools of Mathematics, Computer Science, Geography and Business. Programme leader [Dr Luisa Cutillo](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/maths/staff/5526/dr-luisa-cutillo) researches networks and network applications, including validating network structures and biomedical network applications, and is one of the Women in Machine Learning Boards of Directors. Students may also be taught by industry professionals and trained postgraduate researchers.
Assessment is by a range of methods, including formal examination, assignments, coursework, reports and practical activities.
There is increasing demand for individuals who can manage and control the way data is used. Data scientists are increasingly important in helping governments, businesses, researchers, NGOs and other organisations make sense of growing amounts of information. University of Leeds students are among the top 5 most targeted by top employers according to [The Graduate Market 2024, High Fliers Research](https://online.flippingbook.com/view/747999993/). Previous data science graduates have secured roles including Product SME at Shell UK, Senior Software Engineer at London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG), and Data Integration Lead at Stainless Games.
While studying at Leeds, students have the opportunity to complete an eight-week [virtual work experience](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Fwork-experience&data=05%7C02%7CB.Cairney%40leeds.ac.uk%7Cd370f21983754013f75008dddb4ffad7%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638907858738083812%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=dvWiCk8T2J7H9dGR3nbAmyvRxD5fVNGRuJ2w7%2F0R6Oo%3D&reserved=0), working on a project aligned with their academic discipline and partnered with a relevant company. The work experience is formally integrated into the degree, enabling students to graduate with an MSc with Work Experience.

Curriculum.content:
Start date: September 2026. Delivery type: On campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
The course will equip you with the knowledge and skills you need to meet the challenges of data science in the modern world. You can choose modules from the School of Mathematics, the School of Computer Science, the School of Geography and Leeds University Business School. Mathematics modules are available for students who are not from a mathematics/statistics background, while computing modules will be suitable for students on this programme who are not from a computer science background.
Course structure: the list shown below represents typical modules/components studied and may change from time to time.
Compulsory modules:
- **Data Science –15 credits**: This module gives you an insight into some general principles of the work of a data scientist and teaches you some of the underpinnings of artificial intelligence and statistics in the practice of data science.
- **Project skills in Data Science –15 credits**: This module will develop your skills for your project, potential further research, and employment. This will include presentation skills and teamwork, some of which will be developed through real-life case studies.
- **Project in Data Science and Analytics – 60 credits**: The project gives you the opportunity to demonstrate independent research skills necessary for a professional or academic career. It allows you to deepen your knowledge and understanding of practical issues whilst applying skills acquired throughout the programme. The list of topics to choose for your project is wide-ranging, dealing with a real-world problem. It will typically require a literature review, project planning, data collection, analysis and interpretation. Many recent projects have involved co-supervision with the Leeds Clinical Trials Unit, Leeds Institute for Data Analytics (LIDA) and the MET office. It is possible to involve an industrial partner in your dissertation, subject to the approval of the programme manager.
Optional modules are indicative of typical options:
- Machine Learning – 15 credits
- Deep Learning – 15 credits
- Programming for Data Science – 15 credits
- Geographic Data Visualisation & Analysis – 15 credits
- Big Data and Consumer Analytics – 15 credits
- Business Analytics and Decision Science – 15 credits
- Forecasting and Advanced Business Analytics – 15 credits
- Machine Learning in Practice – 15 credits
- Statistical Theory – 15 credits
- Statistical Theory and Methods – 15 credits
- Statistical Learning – 15 credits
- Statistical Computing – 15 credits
- Transport Data Science – 15 credits
Teaching is through lectures, tutorials, seminars and supervised research projects. Assessment is by a range of methods, including formal examination, assignments, coursework, reports and practical activities.
As part of your course, you will have access to the [Professional and Academic Communication module](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Ffaculty-engineering-physical-sciences%2Fdoc%2Fguide-professional-academic-communication-module&data=05%7C02%7CS.Wilson3%40leeds.ac.uk%7C657723c6ba5e4936433308ddd107b250%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638896553169948867%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=rdKf6rUQYbTAMfHoMZQ7w1sQZJ%2FeYamQmwtgwgZIdd8%3D&reserved=0), delivered through a combination of in-person workshops and independent online study.
While studying at Leeds, you’ll have the opportunity to complete an eight-week [virtual work experience](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Fwork-experience&data=05%7C02%7CB.Cairney%40leeds.ac.uk%7Cd370f21983754013f75008dddb4ffad7%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638907858738083812%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=dvWiCk8T2J7H9dGR3nbAmyvRxD5fVNGRuJ2w7%2F0R6Oo%3D&reserved=0), working on a project aligned with your academic discipline and partnered with a relevant company. This practical experience is formally integrated into your degree, enabling you to graduate with an MSc with Work Experience.

Cost of Attendance.content:
The following estimates are for a single student in 2025, based on the latest data available. They do not include tuition fees.

| --- | --- |
| University accommodation, self-catered | £117 to £265 |
| University accommodation, catered | £205 to £273 |
| Private accommodation, self-catered | £110 to £300 (costs may be more for higher specifications) |
| Living expenses | Estimated cost per week |
| --- | --- |
| Groceries: food, toiletries and cleaning products | £31 to £38 |

| Personal costs: transport, socialising, restaurants/takeaways, clothes and mobile phone | £44 to £68 |
**Estimated total budget per week: approximately £199 to £423**

Financial Aid.content:
We have up to £9.4 million worth of scholarships available for international students commencing their studies in September 2026.
- **International Regional Scholarships**: An automatic **£6,000 fee reduction scholarship** is available for international Masters students from an eligible country/region. International Masters Regional Scholarships are automatically awarded to eligible students as a fee reduction.
- Eligibility criteria: passport holder from Egypt, India, Japan, Mexico, Peru, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, Turkey, United States of America, Vietnam; classified as an international fee-paying student; self-funded or partially-funded; hold a conditional or unconditional offer for a Masters degree (including MRes) starting in September 2026.
- You do not need to apply for the International Masters Regional Scholarship. If you meet the eligibility and award criteria, you will automatically receive the scholarship.
- This scholarship award **cannot be deferred** to the following year and is only transferable to other eligible courses at the University of Leeds. It **can be combined** with the International Excellence Scholarship or external funding as long as this does not exceed 100% of your tuition fees. You may also be able to combine this scholarship with a School or Faculty scholarship. This scholarship is paid as a fee reduction for your first year of study only and can only be used as a fee reduction; it **cannot be used** towards other costs, including but not exclusive to maintenance or accommodation costs.
- **International Excellence Scholarships**: 500 scholarships, worth either **£3,000, £6,000 or £16,000**, are available to support eligible international students. The awards recognise and reward high academic achievement for students applying to study a taught Masters course starting in September 2026. Applications for the International Excellence Scholarships are now **closed**.
- Eligibility criteria: classified as an international student for fee purposes; have a conditional or unconditional offer for an eligible taught Masters course starting in September 2026; be self-funded or partially-funded; demonstrate an excellent academic track record, and be predicted to achieve or have achieved a minimum of a Bachelor’s degree with a 2:1 (hons) or equivalent; show excellent professional and personal skills evidenced through work experience and/or extracurricular activities.
- Applications for this scholarship have now **closed**. If you applied by the 29 May deadline, you will be notified of the outcome of your application by 26 June.
- The International Excellence Scholarship **can be combined** with the International Regional Scholarship or external funding as long as this does not exceed 100% of your tuition fees. You may also be able to combine this scholarship with a School or Faculty scholarship. The scholarship award **cannot be deferred** to the following year and is non-transferable to other courses at the University of Leeds. The scholarship is paid as a fee reduction for your first year of study only and can only be used as a fee reduction; it **cannot be used** towards other costs, including but not exclusive to maintenance or accommodation costs.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: Please note that we do not permit deferrals.

Conditional Admission Policy.content: International students who do not meet the English language requirements for this programme may be able to study the University of Leeds postgraduate pre-sessional English course to help improve their English language level. This pre-sessional course is designed with a progression route to the degree programme, and students learn academic English in the context of their subject area. Relevant options include [Language for Science (6 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/i204/language-for-science), [Language for Science: General Science (10 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/i203/language-for-science-general-science), the [six week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j615/online-academic-english-presessional-6-weeks-), the [10 week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j614/online-academic-english-presessional-10-weeks-), and longer [postgraduate pre-sessional English courses](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre-courses/doc/masters-pre-sessional-english).
